This page presents the marimo note as a browser-readable Quarto document. Run the `.py` file locally with marimo to execute its cells.

```{.python}
import marimo

__generated_with = "0.17.2"

app = marimo.App()


@app.cell
def _():
    from pathlib import Path

    import marimo as mo
    import polars as pl
    import pyreadr
    import statsmodels.api as sm
    from great_tables import GT
    from scipy.stats import f_oneway
    from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

    return GT, Path, f_oneway, mo, ols, pl, pyreadr, sm


@app.cell
def _(Path, pl, pyreadr):
    data_path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "Stat2Data" / "FatRats.rda"
    rda_objects = pyreadr.read_r(str(data_path))
    data = pl.from_pandas(rda_objects["FatRats"])

    data.head()
    return data, data_path


@app.cell
def _(data, pl):
    high_protein = data.filter(pl.col("Protein") == "Hi")

    summary = (
        high_protein.group_by("Source")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("n"),
            pl.col("Gain").mean().alias("mean_gain"),
            pl.col("Gain").std().alias("sd_gain"),
        )
        .sort("Source")
    )
    summary
    return high_protein, summary


@app.cell
def _(GT, summary):
    GT(summary.to_pandas())
    return


@app.cell
def _(f_oneway, high_protein, mo):
    groups = [
        high_protein.filter(high_protein["Source"] == source)["Gain"].to_numpy()
        for source in ("Beef", "Cereal", "Pork")
    ]
    test = f_oneway(*groups)
    mo.md(
        f"**One-way ANOVA:** $F = {test.statistic:.4f}$, "
        f"$p = {test.pvalue:.4f}$"
    )
    return groups, test


@app.cell
def _(high_protein, ols, sm):
    model = ols("Gain ~ C(Source)", data=high_protein.to_pandas()).fit()
    anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=1)
    anova_table
    return anova_table, model


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```
